title: Ordinary transposes of augmented copower resolutions represent normalized derived counits
statement:
Let $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories in [def-weil-size-convention], with the topology generated by singleton identity coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix a commutative ring $R$ and write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal C}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$ for module presheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $g^{-1}$ be precomposition with $u$ and $g_!=\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{op}}$ its left adjoint. Use the canonical everywhere-defined total left derived functor $Lg_!$, comparison $\varepsilon_C:Lg_!QC\to Qg_!C$ and normalized adjunction of [lem-trf-continuous-cocontinuous-derived-shriek], with $Q$ the localization of complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use coefficient representables from [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic]. Let $K\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal D}$ and let $\alpha:C\to g^{-1}K[0]$ be a quasi-isomorphism of presheaf complexes, where $C^r=0$ for $r>0$ and $\varepsilon_C$ is invertible. Suppose a small-family decomposition $C^0\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J}L_{U_j}^{\mathcal E}(M_j)$ is specified. Let $f_j:M_j\to K(uU_j)$ be the restriction of $\alpha^0_{U_j}$ to the identity summand, so $\alpha^0_W(t,x)=K(u(t))f_j(x)$ on the $j$th summand. Let $c:g_!C\to K[0]$ be the ordinary adjoint of $\alpha$. Then $c$ is zero outside degree zero and on the canonical Kan coordinates of [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic] it is
$$c^0_V(j,t:V\to uU_j,x)=K(t)f_j(x).$$
This formula annihilates the differential from degree $-1$. Write $e_K:Lg_!g^{-1}Q(K[0])\to Q(K[0])$ for the canonical derived counit, identifying exact precomposition with its termwise derived functor. Then
$$e_K\circ Lg_!Q(\alpha)=Q(c)\circ\varepsilon_C,\qquad e_K=Q(c)\circ\varepsilon_C\circ(Lg_!Q\alpha)^{-1}.$$
These equalities are for the actual normalized derived adjunction, with no arbitrary automorphism of either side. At each $V$ the resulting counit representative is the localized displayed chain map. For $s:V'\to V$ its restriction equality is $K(s)c_V=c_{V'}(g_!C)(s)$. If $\alpha':C'\to g^{-1}K'[0]$, $q:K\to K'$ and $v:C\to C'$ satisfy $\alpha'v=g^{-1}q\,\alpha$, their ordinary adjuncts satisfy $q[0]c=c' g_!(v)$, and the derived representatives satisfy the same equality under the canonical comparisons. In particular on generators restriction is $K(ts)f_j(x)=K(s)K(t)f_j(x)$, and coefficient naturality is $q_VK(t)f_j(x)=K'(t)q_{uU_j}f_j(x)$.

proof.text: Write $T=g^{-1}$. On the identity-cover sites all presheaves are sheaves. For the degree-zero summand $L_{U_j}^{\mathcal E}(M_j)$, the natural representing bijection identifies its map to $TK$ with $f_j:M_j\to K(uU_j)$; its value at $(a:W\to U_j,x)$ is therefore $K(u(a))f_j(x)$. A left adjoint preserves a specified sum directly: maps from its image into $H$ correspond to maps from the sum into $TH$, hence to families of maps from its summands into $TH$, hence to families from their images into $H$. Thus the specified decomposition and $g_!L_{U_j}^{\mathcal E}(M_j)\cong L_{uU_j}^{\mathcal D}(M_j)$ identify $g_!C^0$ with the sum of these latter copowers. The representing bijections on both sides, natural in $H$, send an adjunct to the same $f_j$. Consequently its degree-zero component is $c^0_V(j,t,x)=K(t)f_j(x)$.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories; elementary coefficient-representable adjunct calculation.

proof.text: Transpose $\alpha^0:C^0\to TK$ to obtain $c^0:g_!C^0\to K$. The transpose of $c^0g_!(d_C^{-1})$ is $\alpha^0d_C^{-1}=0$, since $\alpha$ is a chain map into $TK[0]$; naturality of transposition with the zero endomorphism of the target shows that the transpose of zero is zero, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $c^0g_!(d_C^{-1})=0$. Set $c^r=0$ for $r\ne0$. This proves every chain-map equation: the only possibly nonzero one is the equation just checked. Componentwise transposition gives $\alpha$, so this is the ordinary adjunct $c$ in the statement. This also proves that the displayed formula annihilates the incoming differential without any projectivity assumption on $M_j$.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories; elementary coefficient-representable adjunct calculation.

proof.text: For the identity-cover topologies, every covering sieve is maximal and is generated by an identity. Its pullbacks and its image under $u$ are again maximal; the pullback squares for identity coverings are identities. Thus $u$ is continuous. For cocontinuity, refine any covering of $u(U)$ by its identity and use the identity covering of $U$. The constant ring pulls back to the same constant ring, so the structural ring map is the identity. Use the normalized derived adjunction bijection of the cited lower-shriek theorem with $N=K[0]$ and the chain map $c$. It sends $Q(c)\varepsilon_C$ to $Q(\alpha)$. By definition its counit $e_K$ corresponds to the identity of $TQ(K[0])$. Naturality of this same bijection in its first variable shows that $e_K\circ Lg_!Q(\alpha)$ also corresponds to $Q(\alpha)$. Its injectivity gives $e_K\circ Lg_!Q(\alpha)=Q(c)\varepsilon_C$. The quasi-isomorphism $\alpha$ becomes an isomorphism under $Q$, and a functor preserves inverses, so right composition by $(Lg_!Q\alpha)^{-1}$ gives the second equality. Both sides use the stipulated normalized bijection, so the calculation introduces no choice of automorphism.

proof.text: For $s:V'\to V$, restriction in the copower coordinates sends $(j,t,x)$ to $(j,ts,x)$. Hence $c^0_{V'}(j,ts,x)=K(ts)f_j(x)=K(s)K(t)f_j(x)=K(s)c^0_V(j,t,x)$. Linearity and the universal property of the direct sum give the restriction equality on all sections; in every other degree both maps are zero. Evaluation is exact here: the module-category definition computes kernels sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying sectionwise cokernels, while every presheaf on the identity-cover site is already a sheaf. It therefore preserves quasi-isomorphisms and factors through localization. Applying this factorization to step 3 identifies the evaluated counit, via the isomorphism $\varepsilon_C(Lg_!Q\alpha)^{-1}$, with the localization of the displayed chain map $c_V$.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories; elementary coefficient-representable adjunct calculation.

proof.text: Let $v,q,\alpha'$ satisfy the stated square, and let $c'$ be the adjunct of $\alpha'$. Naturality of ordinary transposition sends $q[0]c$ to $Tq[0]\alpha$, and $c'g_!(v)$ to $\alpha'v$. These are equal by hypothesis; injectivity gives $q[0]c=c'g_!(v)$. Localizing this equation and using comparison naturality $Qg_!(v)\varepsilon_C=\varepsilon_{C'}Lg_!Q(v)$ yields $Q(q[0])Q(c)\varepsilon_C=Q(c')\varepsilon_{C'}Lg_!Q(v)$, the required equality of the derived representatives. When written using the inverted augmentation identifications of step 3 the same equation follows by composing with their inverses. On a generator coefficient naturality is explicitly $q_VK(t)f_j(x)=K'(t)q_{uU_j}f_j(x)$, which is the naturality square of the presheaf morphism $q$ at $t$. It needs no assumption that $v$ preserves the chosen decompositions.
